definitions.gloss: Ogata Kōrin, Edo-period painter and designer
definitions.explanation: A painter and designer of the Edo period (1658–1716) from a Kyoto merchant family, the central figure of the Rinpa school. Known for bold, decorative compositions on folding screens, often with gold leaf, and for designs on lacquerware and kimono.

notes:
Often called simply {光琳|こうりん}. His name gave the Rinpa school its name ({琳派|りんぱ}, which takes its first kanji from {光琳|こうりん}), and his flat, patterned style later influenced European art.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- {燕子花図屏風|かきつばたずびょうぶ}: "Irises", a pair of gold-leaf screens (a National Treasure)
- {紅白梅図屏風|こうはくばいずびょうぶ}: "Red and White Plum Blossoms", a pair of screens (a National Treasure)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {光琳模様|こうりんもよう}: Kōrin patterns, stylized motifs used on kimono and crafts
- {光琳|こうりん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧: Kōrin's plum, a rounded, simplified plum blossom design

RELATED WORDS:
His younger brother {尾形乾山|おがたけんざん} was a celebrated potter, and the two sometimes worked together.
